card.title: Make It Official
card.instruction: Recruit someone by giving them a title, role, or ceremonial duty that makes participation feel binding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you be honorary patron of our roof appeal? You'd open it and thank the donors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can come, but I won't make a speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then accept the patron's ribbon and lead the applause. That can be your ceremonial duty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I leave after the first donation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The patron applauds every donor. We couldn't have the later ones thinking their money mattered less.

mechanism: A gives a willing attendee a ceremonial patron role that turns limited participation into continuing donor acknowledgment.
confusable: Unlike asking for a favor alone, the official identity must make stopping feel like neglecting a duty.
comparison: A ribbon and equal applause bind the patron, unlike the lantern keeper's succession requirement.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
